Alex —

Thanks for the clear list. We're happy to compile this. High-level answers up front:
- We support TLS 1.2 and 1.3 on the public API endpoints; TLS 1.3 is preferred and newly negotiated connections default to 1.3 when the client supports it.
- For TLS 1.2 we only permit a small set of AEAD ciphers (AES-GCM and CHACHA20-POLY1305 equivalents); RSA key-exchange ciphers are not enabled.
- Private TLS keys for the load balancers and service mTLS certificates are stored in a customer-segregated HSM cluster (FIPS 140-2 level 2/3 depending on region) and we use KMS-wrapped keys for application-level envelopes.
- Rotation cadence: we maintain a rolling schedule for leaf TLS certs every 90 days, intermediate KEKs rotated quarterly, and rewrap windows for application KEKs in a staggered monthly pattern per-region to avoid simultaneous full-cluster rekeying.

I'll attach a short CSV export of the cipher inventory and a PDF that sketches the staggered rekey plan. Marissa, Irene — could you review the HSM operator separation diagram I drafted and confirm it matches our current practice (separation of duties, access windows, and key ceremony notes)?

I'll assemble a single ZIP for you by EOD tomorrow. If Jan 6 is firm we'll hit it.

Thanks,

Clarifications:

Alex / ClearShore team —

Please find the requested artifacts attached and summarized below. We bundled everything into a short packet to make intake easier for auditors:

1) cipher-inventory.csv (attached) — row per endpoint: hostname, port, TLS versions, allowed ciphers, preferred_order.
2) staged-rekey-plan.pdf (attached) — shows the 12-month staggered schedule by region and service, planned dates, rollback windows, and expected impact (no more than 2% traffic migration during any single rekey window).
3) hsm-operator-separation.png (attached) — a compact diagram showing operator role split, emergency unseal steps, audit log retention (90 days live, 7 years archived), and who has manual auth token privileges.

Notes/highlights:
- TLS 1.3 is enforced for new sessions where clients advertise support; we will not accept legacy RSA-KEX cipher suites for TLS 1.2.
- Root HSMs are in FIPS-validated modules; the HSM cluster is maintained by a narrow operator group separate from service ops and product engineers. Access requires multi-person authorization for high-impact actions.
- We perform scheduled KEK rotations quarterly; application KEKs are rewrapped monthly in a rolling per-region window to avoid single-point bulk rotation.
